title: How to Spot a Fake Email
sources: FBI IC3, 2024 Internet Crime Report (phishing/spoofing was the most reported crime type: 193,407 complaints)
Microsoft Support, 'Protect yourself from phishing' (check the sender's real address, not only the display name; hover over a link to see where it really goes)
FTC Consumer Advice, 'How to Recognize and Avoid Phishing Scams' (scammers create urgency: act now, your account will be closed)
FTC Consumer Alerts on verification-code scams (a code is only for you; anyone who asks you for it is a scammer)

lines.text: In twenty twenty-four, the FBI got almost two hundred thousand phishing complaints,
lines.caps: In *2024, | the *FBI got | almost *200,000 | phishing complaints

lines.text: so here's how to spot a fake email in four quick checks.
lines.caps: So here's how | to spot a *fake email | in *4 quick checks

lines.text: One, look at the real sender address, not just the name,
lines.caps: 1. Look at the | real *sender address, | not just the *name

lines.text: because anyone can call themselves your bank.
Two, hover over the link before you click it,
lines.caps: 2. *Hover over | the link before | you *click it

lines.text: and make sure it goes where it says it does.
lines.caps: and make sure | it goes where | it *says it does

lines.text: Three, watch out for pressure, like act now or lose your account.
lines.caps: 3. Watch out for | *pressure, | like act now | or *lose your account

lines.text: That panic is exactly what they want.
And four, never send a password or a login code by email.
lines.caps: And 4. *Never | send a *password | or a login *code | by email

lines.text: Anyone who asks for one is running a scam.

lines.text: Send this to the friend who clicks every link.
